text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Jack Calamatta, general secretary of the General Workers Union said in interview it was former Malta Drydocks council chairman, Sammy Meilaq who said the new council should have a majority of government members. The council is the dockyard's board of directors. It had been directly elected by the workers from among employees for 22 years.
- Prime Minister Alfred Sant complains of apathy and hinderance by supporters of the opposition Nationalist Party in the police force.
- Albanians apply to live in Malta. Some 20 Albanians have applied to live in Malta since the troubles started in their country.
- Young man found dead after overdose.
